title: Language and Communication Accommodations
description: Adjustments to how teachers phrase, pace, and deliver verbal information. Use when the student has difficulty processing language, understands literal language better than figurative, or needs simpler/chunked instructions to comprehend tasks.

source.name: ADayInOurShoes — Ultimate List of IEP Accommodations, Modifications & Strategies (SDIs)

accommodations.text: Minimal use of open-ended statements or questions.
Do not use sarcasm or inferences when communicating with the student.
Allow 5 or 10 seconds (whatever the child needs) of processing time when a request is made.
Use only one question or instruction at a time if the child cannot handle 2- or 3-part questions.
Have someone read the material to them.
Clear, concise instructions at the child's ability level.
Limit oral questions to the number the child can manage.
Provide direct feedback in appropriate settings.
